member.name: M:JCass_MonteCarloModel.Core.MonteCarloModel.ChooseChunkSize(System.Int32)
member.summary: Chooses an appropriate chunk size for batching rows during SQLite bulk inserts.
member.param: Total number of rows that will be inserted for a single parameter.
member.returns: A chunk size (number of rows per batch) optimised for SQLite bulk insert performance, clamped to a safe range to avoid excessive memory usage or transaction overhead.

remarks.para: The strategy aims to divide the total workload into roughly a fixed number of chunks (currently 12), which provides a good balance between:

item.description: Minimising transaction overhead (too many small batches).
Limiting memory pressure from very large batches.
Reducing long-running write locks in SQLite.

remarks.para: The result is clamped to a conservative range (2,000–20,000 rows) which has proven effective for wide Monte Carlo parameter tables (typically 10–30 modelling periods per row).

member.name: M:JCass_MonteCarloModel.Core.MonteCarloModel.ChooseTrancheSize(System.Int32,System.Nullable{System.Int32})
member.summary: Chooses an appropriate tranche size (degree of parallelism) for running Monte Carlo simulations concurrently.
member.param: Total number of simulations to run.
Optional hard upper limit on the tranche size. This is useful to cap resource usage such as the number of concurrent SQLite databases or file handles.
member.returns: The number of simulations that should be executed in parallel for a single tranche.

remarks.para: The tranche size is primarily CPU-bound and is therefore derived from the number of logical processors available on the machine. One core is intentionally left free where possible to maintain OS and UI responsiveness.
The final tranche size is the minimum of:

item.description: The total number of simulations remaining.
The effective CPU parallelism (processor count minus one).

remarks.para: This approach provides stable, predictable performance for CPU-heavy Monte Carlo workloads while avoiding excessive context switching or resource contention.

member.name: T:JCass_MonteCarloModel.Exporting.SqliteDbMerger
member.summary: Utility for merging multiple SQLite database files (with identical table schemas) into a single master database.
member.remarks: Strategy: 1) Choose a master database path (masterDbPath). 2) If the master DB does not exist, seed it by COPYING the first source DB in sourceDbPaths: - The first DB becomes the base "master" file (schema, indexes, pragmas, etc. are preserved). - That seed DB is then removed from the merge list so its rows are not inserted twice. - After the merge completes successfully, the original seed DB file is deleted (optional). 3) For each remaining source DB: - ATTACH it to the master connection (autocommit mode). - INSERT rows into each table (inside a transaction for atomicity). - DETACH (must be outside the transaction). - Optionally delete the source DB file and its sidecar files (-wal/-shm/-journal).

member.summary: Merge multiple SQLite databases into a single master database using ATTACH + INSERT INTO ... SELECT ..., then optionally deletes the temporary source databases (including WAL/SHM sidecar files).
member.param: The destination SQLite file path. If it does not exist, the first source DB is copied to this path to seed the master.
Source database file paths to merge. These are expected to have identical table structures.
Table names to merge. Each table must exist in both master and source databases.

Optional map of table name to identity/autoincrement column name to exclude from insert (e.g., { "MyTable" : "Id" }). If a table is not present in this dictionary, all columns are inserted for that table.

If true, deletes each source DB after it is merged, including sidecar files (-wal/-shm/-journal). Also deletes the seed DB used to create the master (if master was created by copying the first source).
member.returns: A task representing the asynchronous merge operation.
member.exception: Thrown when is null or empty.
Thrown if insertable columns cannot be resolved for a table.
